newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bolsa recovers to close slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bolsa recovers to close slightly up.

text.p: Argentine stocks on Wednesday reversed losses during the session and closed slightly higher in a technical rebound in line with foreing markets, dealers said.

"Both stocks and debt went along with the rest of the markets," Horacio Bonavia, trader for Portfolio brokers said. "With the exception of Venezuela, everything danced at the rythm of the Dow Jones. Basically there was a change in the regional trend, including the U.S. market, which had opened lower and later pared losses," C&E consultants' chief economist Agustin Etchebarne said.
The leading blue-chip Merval stock index closed 1.19 percent higher at 560.98 points after having fallen about one percent during the day.
Trading volumes rose to $19.3 million in the session.

"Prices were getting a strong support around the 550 level of MerVal," an analyst for a foreign bank said. "Today we saw orders from abroad and the Cavallo issue is basically diminishing. The market should start discounting corruption news and may start going up towards the 570 level in coming days."
The analyst was referring to ongoing bickering between former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo and government officials over his charges of corruption.
But other traders said the market will closely follow the volatile domestic front.
"If the political landscape doesn't change it may be tough for the market," Bonava said. "The market will keep an eye on Cavallo's agenda, where he goes, what he says."
"The market was also encouraged by low prices of Argentine telecoms ADRs at the opening of the U.S. market and pension funds saw a good opportunity to buy," a trader said.
Etchebarne said there was strong support at the 550 point level and that the rebound in Argentina was stronger as stocks had fallen harder than in other markets.
